history.summary: PROVISIONAL IDENTITY: no separate 'Kesaria Rama Temple' has a web footprint; the only Rama temple at Kesaria is the under-construction Virat Ramayan Mandir, so the CSV row is mapped here. If the CSV intended a smaller older shrine in Kesaria town, this mapping is wrong (verify). The project, by the Mahavir Mandir Trust, Patna (spearheaded by the late Acharya Kishore Kunal), was conceived as the world's largest Ramayana temple complex: model unveiled by CM Nitish Kumar in 2013, earlier plans delayed after Cambodia objected to an Angkor Wat-inspired design, construction began June 2023. Planned: 270-ft main shikhar, 33-ft/210-tonne monolithic granite Sahasralingam (installed Jan 2026), 18 shrines on ~120-200 acres at Janaki Nagar near Kaithwalia-Bahuara on the Kesariya-Chakia road; partial opening targeted for Ram Navami 2027 (verify). CSV town 'Motihari' corrected to Kesaria (actual site, ~35-40 km west of Motihari).

name: Kesaria Rama Temple
town_description: Kesaria is a historic town in East Champaran district, Bihar, famous for the Kesariya Buddhist stupa, one of the tallest and largest stupas in the world (104 ft), also known locally as Raja Ben ka Deora. The town sits on the historic Ram-Janaki path and is currently in the news for the under-construction Virat Ramayan Mandir complex nearby. It lies roughly 110-120 km north of Patna.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism, with Shaiva shrines in the complex)

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna, ~120 km
travel.railway: Nearest station: Chakia (verify), ~10-15 km; Motihari Junction is the nearest major station
travel.road: Site at Janaki Nagar near Kaithwalia-Bahuara on the Kesariya-Chakia road; connected via Motihari, Chakia and Raxaul roads

visitor_information.best_time: Not yet open to regular visitors - construction site as of September 2026
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple under construction; partial darshan targeted for Ram Navami 2027 (verify). No public opening hours yet.
